Orden — Arrastre el asa para reordenar. Arriba = primero en la tira del teclado; deslice la tira lateralmente para más páginas.

Restablecer — Tras confirmar, restaura los Favoritos del perfil integrado activo a los valores predeterminados de instalación inicial. Los perfiles personalizados o importados no admiten restablecer. Listo guarda; Cancelar descarta el orden provisional.

Sequence — Type text and tokens in Macro sequence. Use Insert tokens for modifiers, keys, and delays. Match opening and closing tags (e.g. <CTRL> … </CTRL>).
Timing — Send char interval sets delay between keystrokes when the macro runs.
Scheduler — Optional: pick a run time and repeat options. Tap Save when finished.
Where it saves — The shortcut is added to General in Shortcut Hub and to your Favorites strip. To change the name, icon, or order, open Shortcut Hub.

Keys — Toggle modifiers, then tap one letter or key chip. Chips wrap to more lines on small screens. Advanced lets you type token syntax (e.g. <CTRL>c</CTRL>) instead; choosing a chip clears Advanced.

Modifiers & Target OS — Button labels match your current Target OS (header in the main app). The first toggle is ⌘ / Win / Super (HID Gui), then Ctrl, Shift, and Opt / Alt. Stored shortcuts use the same bits as the keyboard; when you change Target OS, labels and HID mapping update together.

Toque para hacer clic con el botón derecho.\nDeslícese con dos dedos para desplazarse.
Un dedo: mover, tocar, doble toque; mantener pulsado para arrastrar (otro toque para soltar).\nDos dedos: desplazamiento; levantar ambos sin deslizar: clic derecho.
Panel: solo mover el puntero y desplazamiento con dos dedos.\nI, C, D: clics y arrastre. Mantenga un botón y deslice hacia arriba para bloquear.
Panel: todos los gestos y desplazamiento con dos dedos.\nFranja: I, C, D + bloqueo. Los toques en el panel hacen parpadear la tecla; al arrastrar desde el panel, I permanece resaltado.

Sends a real modifier-down to the connected device when you long-press, and keeps it applied after each chorded key until you lift your finger. Turn off only if your host misbehaves with sustained modifiers.
Hold modifier on target while chording
Hold key down on the target
Sends one key-down when you press and releases when you lift your finger. Better for games or apps that expect a real held key instead of repeated taps.
After a short delay, sends many quick press-and-release cycles—similar to auto-repeat when holding a physical key for typing.
Short tap sends that modifier key once to the target. Long-press a modifier, keep your finger down, then tap other keys to chord (e.g. long-press Shift and tap 1 for !). Release the modifier to stop.
Tap once to latch a modifier on; tap again to turn off. Highlighted keys show what is latched. Good for typing shifted symbols with a separate tap on Shift, then the key.
